correctness.rationale: From the 12 arcs and their explicit adjacency, full face enumeration gives 163 faces, and a deterministic 78-pair matching on 162 nonempty faces leaves one vertex plus five triangles. All 432 Hasse incidences are oriented and a complete topological-sort visits all 162 nodes, rigorously proving acyclicity for this finite object. Forman yields wedge of five 2-spheres integrally. Signed augmented Lefschetz traces of all 24 S4 elements give (5,-1,1,2,1), equal to 1+sgn(g)Fix(g); rational semisimplicity identifies the module. Each group element has an invariant independent face (checked exhaustively and argued by cycle type); Armstrong and finite-group transfer yield all subgroup quotient conclusions. No inference from partial finite samples or homology rank alone.

value.rationale: The once-subdivided tetrahedron is a natural symmetric graph, and this exact homotopy computation provides a topological benchmark at a non-simplicial-vertex polyhedral example. Crucially the result computes more than a numerical Betti rank: its full S4 character is 1 plus a sign-twisted permutation character, and a fixed-face argument uniformly determines fundamental groups and rational Betti ranks of every subgroup quotient. These data distinguish equivariant and quotient topological structure invisible to the five-sphere homotopy type and have clear use in matching-complex and equivariant-topology comparisons.
